title: Sum of Array
description: Given an array of numbers, return the sum of all elements. The sum of an empty array is 0.
constraints: 0 <= nums.length <= 1000. Each number is between -10^6 and 10^6.
hints: Keep a running total that starts at 0.
Loop over every element and add it to the total.

title: Clamp Value
description: Return n limited to the range from lo to hi (inclusive). If n is below lo return lo, if n is above hi return hi, otherwise return n.

examples.explanation: 15 is above the maximum, so the result is 10.

constraints: -10^9 <= n, lo, hi <= 10^9 and lo <= hi.
hints: Compare n with lo first.
Then compare n with hi. If neither limit applies, return n unchanged.

title: Leap Year Check
description: Return true if the given year is a leap year in the Gregorian calendar. A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except years divisible by 100, unless the year is also divisible by 400.

examples.explanation: 1900 is divisible by 100 but not by 400.
2000 is divisible by 400.

hints: Start with the divisible-by-4 rule.
Handle the century exceptions: divisible by 100 is not a leap year unless divisible by 400.

title: Digital Root
description: Repeatedly replace n with the sum of its digits until it has only one digit, then return that digit.
hints: Extract digits with n % 10 and Math.floor(n / 10).
Repeat the digit sum while the number still has two or more digits.

title: Greatest Common Divisor
description: Return the greatest common divisor of two non-negative integers a and b. gcd(a, 0) is a.

examples.explanation: 6 is the largest number dividing both 12 and 18.

constraints: 0 <= a, b <= 10^9 and a, b are not both 0.
hints: Euclid's idea: gcd(a, b) equals gcd(b, a % b).
Stop when the second number becomes 0.

title: Ordinal Suffix
description: Return the number followed by its English ordinal suffix, for example 1 becomes "1st", 2 becomes "2nd", 3 becomes "3rd" and 4 becomes "4th". Numbers ending in 11, 12 or 13 always use "th".

examples.explanation: 11 is a special case and uses th.
Ends in 2 and is not 12.

hints: Look at n % 100 first to catch 11, 12 and 13.
Otherwise use n % 10: 1 is st, 2 is nd, 3 is rd, everything else is th.

title: Base Converter
description: Convert a non-negative integer n to its representation in the given base (2 to 16). Use uppercase letters A-F for digits above 9. Do not add prefixes or leading zeros; 0 is "0".
hints: Repeatedly take n % base to get the lowest digit.
Build the string from the right, dividing n by the base each time, and special-case 0.

title: Trailing Zeros in Factorial
description: Return the number of trailing zeros in n! (n factorial). n can be large, so do not compute the factorial.

examples.explanation: 25! has 6 factors of 5 (5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 counts twice), giving 6 trailing zeros.

hints: A trailing zero comes from a factor of 10 = 2 * 5, and factors of 2 are plentiful.
Count factors of 5: add n/5, n/25, n/125, ... (integer division).

title: Title Case Words
description: Return the string with the first letter of every word uppercased and the remaining letters lowercased. Words are separated by single spaces; keep all spaces exactly as they appear in the input.

examples.explanation: Each word starts with a capital and the rest is lowercase.

constraints: 0 <= s.length <= 1000. s contains letters and spaces only.
hints: Split on " " so that extra spaces produce empty pieces you can keep.
For each non-empty word combine word[0].toUpperCase() with word.slice(1).toLowerCase(), then join with " ".

title: Camel to Snake Case
description: Convert a camelCase identifier to snake_case: before every uppercase letter that is not the first character insert an underscore, then lowercase every letter.

examples.explanation: Underscores go before V and N.

hints: Walk through the characters one at a time.
An uppercase letter at index 0 gets no underscore; later ones get "_" plus the lowercase letter.

title: Caesar Cipher
description: Shift every letter of s forward in the alphabet by shift positions, wrapping around from z to a. shift may be negative (shift backward). Keep the case of each letter and leave non-letters unchanged.

examples.explanation: H becomes K, e becomes h, and so on; punctuation is unchanged.

hints: Use charCodeAt and String.fromCharCode, working relative to "a" or "A".
JavaScript's % can be negative, so normalise with ((x % 26) + 26) % 26.

title: Isogram Check
description: Return true if no letter appears more than once in s. Ignore case (A and a are the same letter) and ignore every character that is not a letter. The empty string is an isogram.

examples.explanation: Every letter is different.
The letter s appears twice.

hints: A Set remembers which letters you have already seen.
Lowercase the string and skip characters outside a-z.

title: Version Number Compare
description: Compare two version strings made of dot-separated non-negative integers. Return -1 if v1 is older than v2, 1 if v1 is newer, and 0 if they are equal. Compare segment by segment as numbers (so "1.10" is newer than "1.2"), and treat missing segments as 0.

examples.explanation: 2 < 10 in the second segment.
The missing segment counts as 0.

constraints: Each version has 1 to 10 segments; each segment is an integer between 0 and 10^6 and may have leading zeros.
hints: Split both strings on "." and convert the pieces to numbers.
Loop to the longer length, using 0 when a version has run out of segments.

title: Decode Bracketed Repeats
description: An encoded string uses the rule k[text], meaning text repeated k times. Rules can be nested. Return the decoded string. k is a positive integer and the input is always valid.

examples.explanation: 2[c] is cc, so a2[c] is acc, repeated 3 times.

constraints: 1 <= s.length <= 100. s has lowercase letters, digits and brackets. The decoded length is at most 1000.
hints: Use two stacks: one for repeat counts and one for the strings built so far.
On "[" push the current count and string and start fresh; on "]" pop and append the current string repeated count times.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description: Return the longest substring of s that reads the same forwards and backwards. If several have the same length, return the one that starts earliest.

examples.explanation: "bab" and "aba" both work; "bab" starts first.

hints: Every palindrome grows outward from a center: a character or the gap between two characters.
Try each center, expand while both ends match, and keep the result only when it is strictly longer.

title: Text Justification
description: Format an array of words into lines of exactly maxWidth characters, fully justified. Pack as many words as fit on each line (one space minimum between words). Distribute extra spaces between words as evenly as possible, giving the leftmost gaps the extra ones. The last line, and any line with a single word, is left-justified and padded with spaces on the right. Return the array of lines.

examples.explanation: The first line has 3 gaps sharing 8 extra spaces evenly.

constraints: 1 <= words.length <= 300, 1 <= words[i].length <= maxWidth <= 100. Words contain no spaces.
hints: Greedily pick the words for a line while total length plus minimum single spaces stays within maxWidth.
For a full line compute spaces = maxWidth - letters, base = floor(spaces / gaps), and the first (spaces % gaps) gaps get one more.

title: Shortest Palindrome by Prepending
description: You may add characters only in front of string s. Return the shortest palindrome you can obtain this way.

examples.explanation: Adding "dcb" in front gives a palindrome, and nothing shorter works.

hints: The answer is reverse(part that is not covered) + s, so find the longest palindromic prefix of s.
Build s + "#" + reverse(s) and use a prefix-function (KMP failure table) to find the longest prefix matching a suffix.

title: Count Positive Numbers
description: Given an array of integers, return the number of positive integers in the array.

examples.explanation: There are three positive numbers.

hints: Zero is not positive, so use a strict comparison.
Keep a counter and increase it for every element greater than 0.

title: Alternating Sign Sum
description: Return nums[0] - nums[1] + nums[2] - nums[3] + ... , alternating the sign starting with plus. The result for an empty array is 0.
constraints: 0 <= nums.length <= 1000. Each number is between -10^6 and 10^6.
hints: The sign depends on whether the index is even or odd.
Add nums[i] at even indices and subtract it at odd indices.

title: Peak Elements
description: Return, in increasing order, the indices of all peaks in nums. An element is a peak if it is strictly greater than both its left and right neighbours. The first and last elements are never peaks.
constraints: 0 <= nums.length <= 1000. Each number is between -10^6 and 10^6.
hints: Only indices 1 to n-2 can be peaks.
Compare nums[i] with nums[i-1] and nums[i+1] using strict greater-than.
